title: Replicating CoT Monitoring on Instruction-Following Refusal Tasks

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifies a real gap: CoT monitoring is only validated for harmful actions, not over-refusals. If monitors are asymmetric, safety protocol design must account for this. Directly relevant to balanced deployment safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: WildGuard and XSTest are public benchmarks with clear categories. Running a CoT monitor on text outputs is straightforward API or local model usage. No complex training or infrastructure needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: construct dataset from public benchmarks, run monitor, compare detection rates across two failure types. Single model, two conditions, clear metric. Fits in 30 hours.
